Task Name: E1 – Access & Roles
Description: Every action in Manih – Grant Management System is done by a known person who sees and does only what their role allows, with data kept separate for each grantor organization.

Task Name: F01 – Staff accounts and secure sign-in
Description:
Each staff member of the Foundation gets an individual account to sign in, so every action in the system is traceable to a known person. The Admin manages accounts without ever deleting history.

Main flow:
1. The user enters email and password and selects Sign in.
2. The system verifies the credentials and that the account is active.
3. The system identifies the user's role and opens the home page of that role.
4. The system records the sign-in with user and time.
5. The user works; every action is recorded under the user's own identity.
6. The user selects Sign out; the system ends the session and shows the sign-in page.

Business rules:
- No grant, charity, financial or staff data is shown before sign-in.
- Accounts are individual; shared accounts are not allowed.
- The user cannot choose or change their own role; it comes from the account.
- Staff are deactivated, never deleted; their past actions keep their name.
- Sign-ins (successful and failed) and account changes are recorded with user and time and cannot be edited.

Detailed BRD: UC01, UC08, UC09

Task Name: S-F01-01 – Sign in and sign out
Description:
As a staff user, I want to sign in with my own email and password, so that I can work in the system under my own identity.

Note: Email must be a valid format; password is masked.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active account, when the user signs in with the correct email and password, then the home page of their role opens.
2. Given a wrong email or password, when the user signs in, then access is refused with the message "Email or password is incorrect" without saying which value was wrong.
3. Given a deactivated account, when the user signs in with correct credentials, then access is refused with the same generic message.
4. Given a signed-in user, when they select Sign out, then the session ends and opening a protected page shows the sign-in page.

Task Name: S-F01-02 – Reset a forgotten password
Description:
As a staff user, I want to reset my password by email, so that I can regain access without calling the Admin.

Note: Link validity period is configurable (default 60 minutes).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the user selects Forgot password and enters an email, when they submit, then the same confirmation message is shown whether or not the email exists.
2. Given an active account, when the reset is requested, then a single-use link valid for 60 minutes is sent to the account email.
3. Given a reset link that was already used or has expired, when it is opened, then the system refuses it and offers to request a new link.

Task Name: S-F01-03 – End inactive sessions
Description:
As the Foundation, I want inactive sessions to end automatically, so that an unattended screen does not expose grant data.

Note: Timeout period is set by the Admin.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a user inactive for longer than the configured period (default 30 minutes), when they perform any action, then they are asked to sign in again.
2. Given the user signs in again after a timeout, then they are returned to the page they were on.

Task Name: S-F01-04 – Add and edit staff accounts
Description:
As an Admin, I want to add staff and edit their details, so that every employee has their own account with the right role.

Note: Fields: name (required, max 100 characters), email (required, unique), role (required, one of the system roles), department (optional).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the Add staff form, when name, email and role are entered and saved, then the account is created as Active and an activation email is sent so the person can set a password.
2. Given an email that already belongs to another account, when the Admin saves, then the system refuses with "This email is already used by another account".
3. Given an empty name, when the Admin saves, then the system shows "Name is required" and nothing is created.
4. Given an existing account, when the Admin changes name, role or department and saves, then the change is shown in the staff list immediately.

Task Name: S-F01-05 – Deactivate and reactivate staff
Description:
As an Admin, I want to deactivate staff who leave, so that they lose access while their history is kept.

Note: There is no delete action for staff accounts.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active staff account, when the Admin deactivates it and confirms, then its status becomes Inactive and the person can no longer sign in.
2. Given a deactivated account, when its past records are opened, then they still show the person's name as the actor.
3. Given the Admin tries to deactivate their own account, then the action is not allowed.
4. Given an inactive account, when the Admin reactivates it, then the person can sign in again with the same role.

Task Name: S-F01-06 – View the access audit trail
Description:
As an Admin, I want to see who signed in and who changed which account, so that I can investigate any access question.

Note: The acting user is always taken from the signed-in identity.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given any successful or failed sign-in, then an audit entry is recorded with the email used, result, date and time.
2. Given any account creation, change, deactivation or reactivation, then an audit entry is recorded with the acting user, date, time and before / after values.
3. Given the audit trail, when the Admin filters by user and date range, then only matching entries are listed, newest first.
4. Given an audit entry, then no user, including the Admin, can edit or delete it.

Task Name: F02 – Role-based workspace
Description:
Each person sees only the menus, pages and actions of their role, and the system enforces this on every page and action. Fixed system roles ship first; editable and custom roles come later (F29).

Main flow:
1. The system shows the menu with only the sections allowed for the user's role.
2. The system opens the home page defined for the role.
3. The user selects a section; the system shows only the tabs and actions the role allows.
4. On every page and action, the system checks the role before showing data or saving.
5. The user completes the allowed action.

Business rules:
- System roles: Admin, Grants Manager, Reviewer, Committee Secretary, Project Manager, Finance, CEO.
- A staff user has exactly one role in the organization.
- Access is enforced by the system on every page and action, not only by hiding menus.
- Blocked access attempts are recorded with user, page and time.
- Department names are unique and up to 100 characters; deleting a department keeps its staff as "No department".

Detailed BRD: UC02, UC11
Ready: Needs decision: Q149 — should system roles be editable? (does not block: fixed roles ship first)

Task Name: S-F02-01 – Menu and home page per role
Description:
As a staff user, I want to see only the sections of my role, so that the system is simple and I do not see what I should not.

Note: The role-to-section mapping is agreed with the business before build and kept as a reference table.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a Reviewer signs in, when the menu appears, then only the sections allowed for Reviewer are listed.
2. Given each of the seven system roles, when a user of that role signs in, then the home page defined for that role opens and is also reachable from the menu.
3. Given a section with several tabs, when the user opens it, then only the tabs allowed for their role are shown.

Task Name: S-F02-02 – Block access outside the role
Description: As the Foundation, I want the system to refuse any page or action outside a user's role, so that hidden menus are not the only protection.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a user opens a page outside their role by direct link, then the system shows "This page is not available for your role" with a link to their home page.
2. Given a user sends a save or approve action outside their role, then the system refuses it and no data changes.
3. Given any refused access, then an entry with user, page or action, and time is recorded in the audit trail.

Task Name: S-F02-03 – Change a user's role
Description:
As an Admin, I want to change a staff member's role, so that their access follows their new responsibilities.

Note: Only the Admin can change roles.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the Admin changes a user's role from Reviewer to Project Manager, when the user performs their next action, then the Project Manager menu and access apply.
2. Given a role change, then pages of the old role are blocked for that user from their next action.

Task Name: S-F02-04 – Manage departments
Description:
As an Admin, I want to maintain the list of departments and assign staff to them, so that staff are organized as in the Foundation's structure.

Note: Department name: required, up to 100 characters, unique in the organization.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a new department name, when the Admin adds it, then it appears in the departments list with 0 members.
2. Given a name that already exists, when the Admin adds it, then the system refuses with "A department with this name already exists".
3. Given a department with staff, when the Admin deletes it, then the system asks for confirmation stating how many staff will be unassigned, and after confirmation those staff show "No department".
4. Given the departments list, then each department shows its number of members and their names.

Task Name: F29 – Custom roles and permissions
Description:
A permission matrix lets the Foundation create its own roles and adjust access to its structure. Every permission change is traceable with before / after values.

Main flow:
1. The Admin selects a role; the system shows its permission matrix by business area with view, write and delete levels.
2. The Admin creates a new role with a name, optionally copying a system role's permissions.
3. The Admin edits the custom role's permissions per permission, per group or all at once.
4. The Admin saves; the system stores the permissions and records each change with before / after values.
5. The Admin assigns the custom role to staff.
6. The new permissions apply to every user with that role from their next action.

Business rules:
- Permission groups: applications and review, finance and payments, projects and evidence, settings.
- Role names are unique in the organization and up to 60 characters.
- System roles are read-only unless Q149 decides otherwise.
- A role assigned to staff cannot be deleted.
- No change may leave a required approval step without any role able to perform it.
- Every role creation, permission change and deletion is recorded with user, time and before / after values.

Detailed BRD: UC10
Ready: Needs decision: Q149 — may system roles be edited, or only custom roles?

Task Name: S-F29-01 – View the permission matrix
Description: As an Admin, I want to see each role's permissions in one matrix, so that I understand who can do what.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a selected role, then the matrix shows each permission grouped by business area with view, write and delete marked Yes or No.
2. Given a system role is selected, then it is labelled "System — read only" and its permissions cannot be changed.

Task Name: S-F29-02 – Create a custom role
Description:
As an Admin, I want to create a custom role, optionally starting from a system role, so that I can match a position that the system roles do not cover.

Note: Role name: required, up to 60 characters, unique.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a unique name and "Copy from: Reviewer", when the Admin creates the role, then it is created with exactly the Reviewer permissions and the message "Role created" is shown.
2. Given an empty name, when the Admin saves, then the system shows "Role name is required".
3. Given a name already used in the organization, when the Admin saves, then the role is not created.

Task Name: S-F29-03 – Edit a custom role's permissions
Description:
As an Admin, I want to grant or remove permissions of a custom role, so that access follows our internal policy.

Note: Removing a sensitive permission (e.g. final approval, payment approval) asks for confirmation.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a custom role in edit mode, when the Admin removes "write" for a permission and saves, then every user with that role loses that action at their next action.
2. Given the Admin selects all permissions of a group, then view, write and delete are set for every permission in that group in one step.
3. Given a change that would leave no role able to perform a required approval step, when the Admin saves, then the system refuses and names the approval step.

Task Name: S-F29-04 – Assign and delete custom roles
Description: As an Admin, I want to assign custom roles to staff and delete unused ones, so that the role list stays clean and accurate.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a custom role exists, when the Admin edits a staff account, then the role list includes it next to the system roles.
2. Given a custom role is assigned to at least one staff member, when the Admin deletes it, then the system refuses with "The role is assigned to staff — change their roles first".
3. Given an unassigned custom role, when the Admin deletes it and confirms, then it is removed from the role list.

Task Name: S-F29-05 – Role change history
Description: As an Admin, I want to see every change to a role, so that permission changes can be audited.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given any role creation, permission change or deletion, then an entry is recorded with user, date, time and the before / after value of each changed permission.
2. Given a role's history is opened, then entries are listed newest first and cannot be edited or deleted.

Task Name: S-F29-06 – Enable or disable a permission for a whole system role
Description:
As an Admin, I want to switch a permission on or off for a whole system role, so that I can adjust access without creating a new role.

Note: Built only if Q149 allows editing system roles.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a permission is disabled for the Finance role, when any Finance user performs their next action, then that permission is no longer available to them.
2. Given a system role was changed, when the Admin selects Restore default permissions and confirms, then the role returns to its original permissions and the change is in the role history.

Task Name: F34 – Multi-organization platform
Description:
Several grantor organizations can use the same Manih platform with strictly separated data. A platform administrator registers, suspends and reactivates grantor organizations.

Main flow:
1. The system lists all grantor organizations with name, official email, number of users, creation date and status.
2. The Platform Administrator selects New organization and enters the name and official email.
3. The system creates the organization as Active and sets up its first Admin account.
4. The Platform Administrator suspends or reactivates an organization after confirmation.
5. The system applies the new status and records the action in the platform audit trail.

Business rules:
- Users of one organization never see or change another organization's data, including in search, exports and reports.
- Organization name is required (up to 120 characters); the official email must be valid.
- Suspension blocks sign-in and new transactions but keeps all the organization's data.
- The organization list shows user counts only, not users' personal data.
- The Platform Administrator does not see an organization's own settings or data by default.

Detailed BRD: UC17
Ready: Needs decision: Is Manih for one foundation or several?

Task Name: S-F34-01 – Register a grantor organization
Description:
As a Platform Administrator, I want to register a new grantor organization with its first Admin, so that it can start using Manih on its own.

Note: Name up to 120 characters; official email in valid format.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a name and a valid official email, when the Platform Administrator saves, then the organization is created with status Active and the message "Organization created" is shown.
2. Given a new organization, when it is created, then an activation email is sent to its first Admin.
3. Given an empty name, when saving, then the organization is not created.

Task Name: S-F34-02 – Suspend and reactivate an organization
Description: As a Platform Administrator, I want to suspend an organization and reactivate it later, so that access can be stopped without losing data.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an Active organization, when the Platform Administrator suspends it and confirms, then its status becomes Suspended and its users cannot sign in.
2. Given a user of a suspended organization tries to sign in, then the message "Your organization is suspended — please contact platform administration" is shown.
3. Given a suspended organization is reactivated, then its users can sign in again and all its data is unchanged.
4. Given any create, suspend or reactivate action, then it is recorded in the platform audit trail with user and time.

Task Name: S-F34-03 – Isolate data between organizations
Description:
As a grantor organization, I want my data to be invisible to other organizations, so that our grants and charities stay confidential.

Note: Applies to every list, search, report, export and assistant answer.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given two organizations A and B, when a user of A searches, lists or exports any records, then no record of B is included.
2. Given a user of A opens a direct link to a record of B, then the system responds as if the record does not exist.

Task Name: S-F34-04 – Restrict platform administration
Description: As the platform owner, I want platform administration to be available only to the Platform Administrator, so that no organization can manage another.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an organization Admin opens the platform organizations page by link, then the system shows "This page is for platform administration only" with a link to their settings.
2. Given the organizations list, then each row shows the number of users but no user names or emails.

Task Name: E2 – Charity Registry
Description: Charities register and manage their own team online, and the Foundation keeps one verified register of Charities so that funding goes only to verified Charities and bank accounts.

Task Name: F03 – Charity self-registration
Description:
A Charity registers online with its licence number, organization data, delegate details and required documents instead of sending papers. The request goes to the Foundation for review and the applicant can follow its status.

Main flow:
1. The visitor enters the charity's licence number and selects Check.
2. The system confirms the licence number is not registered and has no pending request, and opens the registration form.
3. The visitor enters the organization data and the delegate details.
4. The visitor verifies the delegate mobile and the official email with one-time codes.
5. The visitor uploads the required documents (licence, delegate authorization letter).
6. The visitor submits; the system creates a registration request with status Pending and a request number.
7. The visitor follows the request status using the request number.

Business rules:
- One Charity per licence number; duplicate registrations are stopped.
- Mandatory: charity name, licence number, region, city, official email, charity phone, delegate name, delegate national ID (10 digits), delegate mobile.
- Delegate mobile and official email must be verified by one-time code before submission.
- Licence and delegate authorization documents are mandatory.
- No Charity record is created until the Foundation approves the request (F04).
- Identities of existing delegates or requesters are only shown masked.

Detailed BRD: UC39
Ready: Needs decision: Which identity verification is required for delegates (OTP only, or national ID)?

Task Name: S-F03-01 – Check the licence number before registering
Description: As a charity delegate, I want the system to check our licence number first, so that we do not register a charity that already exists.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a licence number that is not registered and has no pending request, when the visitor selects Check, then the registration form opens with the licence number filled in.
2. Given a licence number of a registered Charity, when the visitor selects Check, then the message "This charity is already registered" is shown and no form opens.
3. Given a licence number with a pending request, when the visitor selects Check, then the message "A registration request for this charity is already under review" is shown with the requester's masked name, and no new request can be started.

Task Name: S-F03-02 – Enter charity and delegate details
Description:
As a charity delegate, I want to enter our organization data and my details in one form, so that the Foundation has what it needs to approve us.

Note: Mandatory: charity name, licence number, region, city, official email, charity phone, delegate name, delegate national ID, delegate mobile.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a mandatory field is empty, when the visitor tries to submit, then the field is highlighted and submission is blocked.
2. Given a delegate national ID that is not 10 digits, when the visitor leaves the field, then the message "National ID must be 10 digits" is shown.
3. Given the region field, then it offers only values from the standard region list.

Task Name: S-F03-03 – Verify delegate mobile and official email
Description:
As the Foundation, I want the delegate mobile and official email verified by one-time code, so that we can reach the charity and trust its contact data.

Note: The code is never shown on screen; it is only sent by SMS or email.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the visitor selects Send code for a mobile or email, then a 6-digit code is sent to it and expires after 5 minutes.
2. Given the correct code is entered before it expires, then the field is marked Verified.
3. Given a wrong or expired code, then the message "The code is incorrect or has expired" is shown and the field stays unverified.
4. Given a verified value is changed, then its verification is reset and submission is blocked with "Verify first: <field>".

Task Name: S-F03-04 – Upload required documents
Description:
As a charity delegate, I want to attach our licence and my authorization letter, so that the Foundation can verify the charity and my mandate.

Note: Allowed types PDF, JPG, PNG; maximum 10 MB per file (to be confirmed by IT).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the licence or the delegate authorization letter is missing, when the visitor submits, then submission is blocked with "Attach the required documents: <document>".
2. Given a file that is not PDF, JPG or PNG or is larger than 10 MB, when it is uploaded, then it is refused with a message stating the allowed types and size.
3. Given an uploaded document, then the visitor can view or replace it before submission.

Task Name: S-F03-05 – Submit the request and follow its status
Description: As a charity delegate, I want to submit the registration and see its status, so that I know when we can start using the portal.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given all data is complete and verified, when the visitor submits, then a request is created with status Pending and a request number is shown and sent to the delegate mobile.
2. Given a request number and the delegate mobile, when the visitor opens Registration status and enters the one-time code sent to that mobile, then the current status (Pending, Returned, Approved or Rejected) is shown.
3. Given the request is Returned or Rejected, then the status page shows the Foundation's reason.

Task Name: F04 – Registration review and charity register
Description:
The Grants Manager reviews registration requests and approves, returns or rejects them, so the Foundation keeps one trusted register of approved Charities. Charities can also be added manually and their delegate invited to activate the account.

Main flow:
1. The system lists registration requests, Pending first, with charity name, licence number, date and status.
2. The Grants Manager opens a request and checks the data and documents.
3. The Grants Manager approves the request.
4. The system creates the Charity record with status Active and the delegate's account as primary delegate.
5. The system sends the delegate an activation email to set a password and sign in.
6. The Charity appears in the charity register.

Business rules:
- A reason is mandatory to return or reject a request, and the applicant sees it.
- A Charity is created only by approving a request or by manual addition; never twice for the same licence number.
- Only Pending requests can be decided; each decision is recorded with user and time.
- The register lists only the Foundation's own Charities; exports contain the same rows as the filtered list.
- Activation and invitation links are single-use and time-limited.

Detailed BRD: UC49, UC50, UC56, UC57

Task Name: S-F04-01 – Registration requests queue
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want a queue of registration requests with their documents, so that I can review new Charities in one place.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the queue opens, then Pending requests are listed first with charity name, licence number, submission date and status.
2. Given the Grants Manager filters by status Returned, then only Returned requests are listed.
3. Given a request is opened, then all submitted data, the verified contact fields and each uploaded document are shown and documents can be opened.

Task Name: S-F04-02 – Approve a registration request
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to approve a valid registration, so that the Charity joins the register and its delegate can sign in.

Note: The approval is linked to the created Charity record.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a Pending request, when the Grants Manager approves it, then a Charity record is created with status Active and the request status becomes Approved.
2. Given the approval, then the delegate account is created as primary delegate and an activation email is sent; after setting a password the delegate can sign in to the charity portal.
3. Given the licence number was registered in the meantime, when the Grants Manager approves, then approval is blocked with "A charity with this licence number already exists".

Task Name: S-F04-03 – Return or reject a registration request
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to return a request for correction or reject it with a reason, so that the applicant knows exactly what to do.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the Grants Manager returns or rejects a request without a reason, then the action is blocked with "Reason is required".
2. Given a request is Returned with a reason, then the delegate sees the reason, can correct the data and documents, and resubmits the same request, which becomes Pending again.
3. Given a request is Rejected, then it is closed, no Charity is created and the delegate sees the reason.

Task Name: S-F04-04 – Charity register with search, filters and export
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want a directory of all our Charities with filters and Excel export, so that I can find and analyse Charities quickly.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the register, then each Charity shows name, licence number, region, charity status and account status (Not activated, Invited, Active).
2. Given the user filters by charity status, then only Charities with that status are listed, and summary counts per status are shown above the list.
3. Given a search by name or licence number, then only matching Charities are listed.
4. Given a filtered list, when the user exports to Excel, then the file contains exactly the listed rows and visible columns.

Task Name: S-F04-05 – Add a charity manually and invite its delegate
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to add a Charity directly and invite its delegate, so that known Charities can be onboarded without self-registration.

Note: Invitation only for Charities whose account is not Active.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a licence number already in the register, when the Grants Manager saves a manual Charity, then creation is blocked and the existing Charity is shown.
2. Given a new Charity with name, licence number and a valid official email, when saved, then it is created with account status Not activated and the creation is recorded with user and time.
3. Given the Grants Manager selects Send invitation, then a single-use link valid for 7 days is sent to the official email and the account status becomes Invited; Resend invitation is available afterwards.
4. Given the representative opens a valid invitation and completes verification, then they become the primary delegate and the account status becomes Active.

Task Name: F05 – Charity portal access and team
Description:
Charity users sign in to their own portal, and the primary delegate manages the charity's team without calling the Foundation. People can also ask to join an already registered Charity.

Main flow:
1. The charity user signs in; the system opens the portal home showing the represented Charity and the user's role in it.
2. The primary delegate opens the Team tab; the system lists members, primary delegate first.
3. The primary delegate adds a member with name, email, national ID and role.
4. The system creates the membership and sends the member an activation email.
5. The primary delegate deactivates members who leave.
6. When needed, the primary delegate transfers the primary delegation to another active member with a reason.

Business rules:
- Each Charity has exactly one active primary delegate at all times.
- On the charity side, only the primary delegate can add, deactivate or transfer team members.
- Team roles: Primary delegate, Project Manager, Finance Officer, Member; one membership per person per Charity.
- The primary delegate cannot be deactivated before the delegation is transferred.
- Charity users see only the data of the Charity they represent and never the staff workspace.
- Team changes and delegation transfers are recorded in the Charity's history with user, time and reason.

Detailed BRD: UC40, UC41, UC55
Ready: Needs decision: Can one person belong to more than one charity? (open comment in BRD)

Task Name: S-F05-01 – Sign in to the charity portal
Description: As a charity user, I want to sign in to the charity portal, so that I can work on my charity's behalf.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active charity user, when they sign in, then the portal home opens showing the Charity name and the user's role in it.
2. Given a charity user opens a staff page by link, then access is refused and they are returned to the portal home.
3. Given a staff user opens the charity portal, then the message "This portal is for charities only" is shown.

Task Name: S-F05-02 – Choose the represented charity
Description:
As a charity user who belongs to more than one Charity, I want to choose which Charity I represent, so that I act for the right organization.

Note: Built only if the decision allows one person in several charities; otherwise one membership per person.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a user with memberships in two Charities, when they sign in, then the last selected Charity is represented and a "Currently representing" selector lists both.
2. Given the user selects the other Charity, then all portal pages refresh to show only that Charity's data and the user's role in it.

Task Name: S-F05-03 – Add a team member
Description:
As a primary delegate, I want to add team members with a role, so that colleagues can work in the portal without contacting the Foundation.

Note: Roles offered: Project Manager, Finance Officer, Member.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given name, email, a 10-digit national ID and a role, when the primary delegate adds a member, then an active membership is created and an activation email is sent; after setting a password the member can sign in.
2. Given the person is already a member of this Charity, when added again, then the system refuses with "This person is already a team member".
3. Given a member who is not the primary delegate, when they open the Team tab, then the team is read-only and Add, Deactivate and Transfer are not available.

Task Name: S-F05-04 – Deactivate a team member
Description: As a primary delegate, I want to deactivate members who leave, so that they lose access to our charity's data.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active member, when the primary delegate deactivates them and confirms, then the membership ends with today's date and the person can no longer act for this Charity.
2. Given the primary delegate tries to deactivate themselves, then the system refuses with "The primary delegate cannot be deactivated before the delegation is transferred".
3. Given a deactivated member, then they remain in the team list, dimmed, with their end date.

Task Name: S-F05-05 – Transfer the primary delegation
Description:
As a primary delegate, I want to transfer the delegation to another active member, so that the Charity always has a responsible delegate.

Note: The role kept by the former delegate (Member) is to be confirmed by the business.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active member and a reason, when the primary delegate confirms the transfer, then that member becomes primary delegate and the previous delegate becomes Member immediately and loses delegate rights.
2. Given no new delegate or no reason, when confirming, then the transfer is blocked with "Select the new delegate and state the reason".
3. Given a transfer, then the transfer history shows date, from, to, method (by charity or by Foundation) and reason.

Task Name: S-F05-06 – Request to join a registered charity
Description:
As a person working for a registered Charity, I want to request to join it, so that I can get portal access without creating a duplicate charity.

Note: All four delegate-change fields are mandatory.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the visitor enters the licence number of a registered Charity, then the Charity name and the primary delegate's masked name and mobile ending are shown.
2. Given the visitor selects Send code to delegate and enters the code the delegate gives them, then a join request is created and the primary delegate sees it in the Team tab to accept or refuse.

Task Name: F06 – Charity profile and verification
Description:
Staff see each Charity's full profile and decision history, confirm or block Charities, verify bank accounts and review licence updates. This ensures funding goes only to verified Charities and verified bank accounts.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager opens the Charity profile with data, documents, team and history.
2. The Grants Manager confirms the Charity after checking its data and documents.
3. The primary delegate updates the bank account and uploads the IBAN certificate; the account becomes Unverified.
4. The Grants Manager opens the IBAN certificate, compares it with the entered data and verifies the account.
5. The primary delegate submits a licence update with the licence document.
6. The Grants Manager compares current and requested values with the document and approves the update.
7. Every decision is added to the Charity's history.

Business rules:
- Charity status: Active, Confirmed, Blocked; block and unblock require a reason.
- A blocked Charity cannot submit new applications.
- Any change to bank name, IBAN or IBAN certificate sets the account to Unverified until staff verify it.
- IBAN must be a Saudi IBAN (SA followed by 22 digits).
- Official data (name, licence number, licence expiry) changes only through an approved licence update.
- The Charity history is append-only: each entry has user, time, before / after values and reason.

Task Name: E3 – Annual Plan & Budget
Description: The Foundation manages its annual plan and budget in Manih instead of spreadsheets, so every grant is funded from a known budget line with live and evidenced figures.

Task Name: F07 – Annual plan and budget structure
Description:
The Grants Manager creates the annual plan with its total budget and builds its tree of tracks, items and initiatives with a budget per level. Changes to saved elements need an evidence document and are kept in the plan history, so the plan can serve as the budget source for grant opportunities from day one.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager opens the Annual Plans list and selects New plan.
2. The Grants Manager enters the plan name, year and total budget and saves; the system creates the plan as Active with a unique reference number.
3. The Grants Manager starts an edit session and adds tracks, then items under tracks and initiatives under items, each with a name and a budget.
4. The system assigns hierarchical codes (1, 1.2, 1.2.3) and shows the tree with each level's budget and the plan total.
5. The system warns on any level whose children's budgets exceed its own budget, showing the difference.
6. The Grants Manager selects Save changes; the system lists the pending changes and asks for an evidence document if any saved element was changed.
7. The system saves all changes together, records each one in the plan history and confirms "{n} changes saved".

Business rules:
- A plan requires a name, a year and a total budget of zero or more; levels require a name and a budget of zero or more.
- The tree has three fixed levels: track → item → initiative.
- Structure and header changes are made only inside an edit session and saved all together or not at all.
- Changing or removing an element that was already saved requires one evidence document (PDF, Word, Excel or image, max 10 MB) per save; adding new levels only does not.
- Children exceeding the parent budget is a warning, not a block.
- The plan history is append-only: change, before and after values, user, date and document.

As a Grants Manager, I want to create the annual plan with its name, year and total budget, so that the year's budget is recorded in the system.

2. Given item 1.1 has 2,000,000 SAR and its initiatives total 2,300,000 SAR, then item 1.1 shows the warning "Children exceed budget by 300,000 SAR"

4. Given an edit session with unsaved changes, then changed levels are highlighted and the number of unsaved changes is shown

Task Name: S-F07-04 – Save edits with an evidence document
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want changes to saved plan elements to be saved with an evidence document, so that every budget change is justified.

Note: Accepted types: PDF, Word, Excel, image. One document covers the whole session.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the user changed the budget of a saved level, when they select Save changes, then the system lists the pending changes and requires an evidence document before Save all is enabled
2. Given the session only added new levels, when the user saves, then no document is required
3. Given a document of an unaccepted type or larger than 10 MB, when the user attaches it, then the system rejects it with the reason and does not save
4. Given 3 pending changes and a valid document, when the user selects Save all, then all 3 are saved and the system confirms "3 changes saved"

Task Name: S-F07-05 – Plans list and plan history
Description:
As a Grants Manager or CEO, I want to list the annual plans and see each plan's change history, so that I can find a plan and know who changed what and why.

Note: Filter by year and active status.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given several plans, when the user opens Annual Plans, then only the Foundation's plans are listed, newest year first, with name, year, budget and active status
2. Given a saved change of item 1.1 from 2,000,000 to 2,500,000 SAR, when the user opens the plan history, then it shows the element, before and after values, user, date and a link to open the document
3. Given any history entry, when any user tries to edit or delete it, then no such action is available
4. Given a CEO opens a plan, then the tree and history are visible but New plan and Edit are not offered

Task Name: F24 – Budget monitoring and adjustments
Description:
Every plan level shows live committed, due, paid and available figures from contracts and payments, and authorised staff increase, decrease or transfer budget with evidence. The plan can be locked at year end so no new grants are funded from it.

Main flow:
1. The user opens the plan summary; the system shows for the plan and each level: budget, committed, due, paid and available.
2. The system flags any level whose available balance is negative with "Over budget".
3. The user drills down from a level to the projects and applications charged to it and its sub-levels.
4. The Grants Manager selects Increase, Decrease or Transfer, chooses the level(s), enters the amount and a note and attaches the evidence document.
5. The system validates the operation and applies it to the level, its parent levels and, for increase or decrease, the plan budget in one step.
6. The system records the operation in the financial operations register with a reference number and in the plan history.
7. At year end the Grants Manager locks the plan with the decision document; the plan's items are no longer offered for new links.

Business rules:
- One definition per figure everywhere: committed = signed contract amounts; due = payments in status Due or later and not paid; paid = payments marked Paid (per F23); available = budget − committed.
- A level's figures include all its sub-levels.
- Every adjustment requires an amount greater than zero and an evidence document (PDF, Word, Excel or image, max 10 MB); a transfer keeps the plan budget unchanged.
- Each operation is applied completely or not at all; concurrent operations cannot overwrite each other.
- The operations register and plan history are append-only.
- A locked plan accepts no new opportunities or projects; running projects and their payments continue.

Detailed BRD: UC22, UC23, UC24, UC25

Task Name: S-F24-01 – Live budget figures per plan level
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want each plan level to show committed, due, paid and available amounts, so that I know how much budget is left at any time.

Note: Figures roll up from initiatives to items, tracks and plan.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given item 1.1 has a budget of 2,000,000 SAR, when a contract of 500,000 SAR charged to it is signed, then item 1.1 and its track show committed increased by 500,000 SAR and available reduced by 500,000 SAR
2. Given a payment of 100,000 SAR on that contract is marked Paid, then paid increases by 100,000 SAR on the item, its track and the plan
3. Given committed exceeds a level's budget, then the level shows a negative available amount in red with the flag "Over budget"
4. Given the same plan, then the figures on the plan summary, the tree and the payments register reconcile

Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to open the projects and applications charged to a level, so that I can explain its figures.
Acceptance Criteria:

2. Given a project in the list, when the user selects it, then the project page opens
3. Given the user lacks access to projects, then the counts are shown but the drill-down is not offered

Task Name: S-F24-03 – Increase, decrease or transfer budget with evidence
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to increase, decrease or transfer a level's budget with an evidence document, so that budget changes during the year are controlled.

Note: Transfer requires different source and target levels.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an increase of 300,000 SAR on item 1.1 with a document, when executed, then item 1.1, track 1 and the plan budget each increase by 300,000 SAR and the system confirms "Increase executed"

3. Given a transfer of 100,000 SAR from item 1.1 to item 2.1, when executed, then 1.1 and its track decrease, 2.1 and its track increase and the plan budget is unchanged

Task Name: S-F24-04 – Financial operations register
Description:
As Finance, I want a register of all budget operations, so that every budget change can be traced and audited.

Note: Each operation also appears in the plan history.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given executed operations, when the user opens the register, then increases, decreases and transfers appear in separate tabs with reference number, plan, level(s), amount, user, note, date and document
2. Given a filter by plan, then only that plan's operations are listed
3. Given the user exports the current tab, then the Excel file contains the same rows without document links
4. Given any operation, then it cannot be edited or deleted

Task Name: S-F24-05 – Lock and reopen the plan
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to lock a plan at year end and reopen it if needed, so that no new grants are funded from a closed budget.

Note: The plans list shows a lock icon on locked plans.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active plan, when the user selects Lock plan without attaching the decision document, then the Lock button stays disabled
2. Given a locked plan, when a user links an opportunity or creates a project, then its items are not offered, and existing links remain visible
3. Given a running project on a locked plan, then its payments continue to be processed
4. Given the user reopens a locked plan with a justification document, then the plan is unlocked and both lock and reopen appear in the plan history with user, date and document

Task Name: F25 – Endowments
Description:
The Foundation registers its endowments (funding sources), records their funding and sees each endowment's share of every plan level and its use. This shows which endowment pays for which grants.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager registers an endowment with a name and optional description.
2. Finance records an endowment funding with amount, date and evidence document; the endowment size is updated.
3. The Grants Manager sets which endowments participate in each plan level.
4. The system splits each level's budget among its participating endowments so that shares total 100%.
5. The user opens the endowment report: share, used and available amount per plan and per level, and the projects it funds.

Business rules:
- Endowment size = total of its recorded fundings; fundings cannot be edited or deleted.
- A level uses its own split, otherwise inherits its nearest parent's split; inherited shares are marked "(inherited)".
- Endowment shares of each level total exactly 100%; only active endowments take part.
- With only one active endowment the whole plan counts against it and no split is shown.
- An endowment with fundings or plan shares cannot be deleted.

Task Name: E4 – Grant Opportunities
Description: The Foundation publishes grant opportunities funded from its annual plan, and the right Charities find them and know whether they can apply.

Task Name: F08 – Publish a grant opportunity
Description:
The Grants Manager creates a grant opportunity linked to an annual plan item, builds its application form and publishes it for a reception window. Calls for grants are announced in one place and never exceed the planned budget.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager selects New opportunity and enters name, description, budget, plan item and reception open and close dates.
2. The system checks the budget against the plan item's available budget and saves the opportunity as Draft.
3. The Grants Manager builds the application form (or picks an existing form) with fields and required flags.
4. The Grants Manager publishes the opportunity; its status becomes Published.
5. The system treats the opportunity as open while it is Published and today is within the reception window.
6. When the close date passes, the opportunity stops accepting applications and its status becomes Closed.
7. The opportunity list shows each opportunity's status, window, budget and application count.

Business rules:
- Name, budget greater than zero, plan item and open and close dates (close after open) are required.
- Only items and initiatives (not tracks) of active, unlocked plans can be selected; they are labelled with plan year, code and name.
- Plan item available budget for opportunities = item budget − budgets of its other non-cancelled opportunities.
- Status flow: Draft → Published → Closed; a Draft is never visible to Charities.
- A form used by any opportunity cannot be deleted; changing a form never changes applications already submitted.
- Changes to a published opportunity are recorded with before and after values, user and date.

Detailed BRD: UC13, UC28, UC29, UC30, UC31

Task Name: F09 – Opportunities on the public page and portal
Description:
Published, open opportunities appear on the public landing page and in the Charity portal with a details page. Charities find open grants without contacting the Foundation.

Main flow:
1. The visitor opens the public landing page without signing in.
2. The system lists published opportunities whose reception window is open, with name, short description, budget and closing date.
3. The visitor opens an opportunity; the details page shows description, budget, dates and conditions.
4. The visitor selects Apply now; if not signed in as a Charity user, the system asks them to sign in or register their Charity.
5. A signed-in Charity user sees the same open opportunities in the portal and opens the opportunity there.

Business rules:
- Only opportunities that are Published and within their open and close dates are listed.
- The landing page and details page are available without sign-in.
- Budget is shown in SAR and the closing date is the official close date of the opportunity.

As a Charity user, I want to see open opportunities in my portal, so that I can find grants without leaving my workspace.

Task Name: F10 – Eligibility, partner groups and invitations
Description:
The Grants Manager sets who may apply to each opportunity (applicant type, region, partner groups, named Charities), invites selected Charities privately and limits applications per Charity. Only the right Charities can apply.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager maintains partner groups (name, description, member Charities).
2. On an opportunity, the Grants Manager sets eligibility rules: applicant types, regions, partner groups and named Charities, and the maximum applications per Charity.
3. The system shows a plain-language summary of the targeting; no rules means open to all.
4. The Grants Manager sends invitations to the targeted groups and named Charities not yet invited.
5. In the portal, the Charity sees opportunities it can apply to with "Applied x of y", and others under "Not available to you" with the reasons.
6. An invited Charity opens its personal link, sees the opportunity terms and continues to apply after signing in.

Business rules:
- Each non-empty rule must be met; an empty rule means no restriction.
- Charities named directly or in a targeted group are always eligible; if only named Charities or groups are targeted, all others are ineligible.
- Group membership is evaluated at the time of the check, so membership changes apply to all opportunities using the group.
- The application limit counts non-cancelled applications; default is 1.
- One invitation per Charity and opportunity, with a unique, unguessable link; status Sent → Opened → Applied or Declined, with dates.
- Eligibility, window and limit are checked again at the moment of applying, not only on screen; an invitation does not bypass the reception window.

Detailed BRD: UC32, UC36, UC43, UC58

Task Name: S-F10-01 – Manage partner groups
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to create partner groups and manage their members, so that I can target opportunities to sets of Charities.

Note: Group changes are recorded with user and date.

Task Name: S-F10-04 – Send private invitations
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to invite targeted Charities by email, so that they know about the opportunity and can apply directly.

1. Given 8 targeted Charities of which 3 were already invited, when the user selects "Send invitations (5)", then 5 invitations are emailed and the system confirms "5 invitations sent"

Task Name: S-F10-05 – Respond to an invitation
Description:
As an invited Charity user, I want to open my invitation and apply or decline, so that I can respond quickly.

Task Name: F28 – Configuration library and governance
Description:
Admins and Grants Managers reuse workflow templates and communication templates, maintain reference lists and applicant types, and change sensitive settings only with an evidence document and a permanent history. Setups are reused instead of rebuilt, and every sensitive change is traceable.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager creates a workflow template with stages, time limits, criteria with weights and a pass score.
2. On an opportunity, the Grants Manager applies a template after confirming that its stages and criteria will be replaced.
3. The Grants Manager maintains communication templates (rejection, contract, notification) with placeholders.
4. The Grants Manager maintains reference lists (entity types, regions, target groups) and opens or closes applicant types for registration.
5. To change a sensitive setting, the user starts an edit session, makes the changes and selects Save changes.
6. The system asks for the evidence document and an optional reason, saves the changes and records before and after values, user and time.

Business rules:
- A template is copied into the opportunity, not referenced; later template changes do not alter existing opportunities.
- New templates start with a pass score of 70% and three standard stages of 5 days each; criteria weights must total 100%.
- A template used by any opportunity cannot be deleted.
- Sensitive settings (workflow templates, applicant types, reference lists, communication templates) are read-only outside an edit session and change only with an evidence document.
- The document and the history entry are saved together or not at all; history entries cannot be edited or deleted.
- Reference list values are unique within a list and at most 80 characters.

Detailed BRD: UC14, UC15, UC18, UC34, UC38

Task Name: S-F28-01 – Maintain workflow templates

Task Name: E5 – Applications & Decisions
Description: Charities apply online and Foundation staff review, score and decide every application through clear stages, with each decision recorded and traceable.

Task Name: F11 – Submit a grant application
Description:
A Charity fills the opportunity's application form in the portal, attaches the required documents and submits it, so every application reaches the Foundation complete and in one place. AI pre-fill comes later (F30).

Main flow:
1. The system opens the application form defined for the opportunity.
2. The delegate enters the core data: project title, description, requested amount, duration (days), implementation region and target groups with beneficiary counts.
3. The delegate adds the bill of quantities (item, quantity, unit price) where the opportunity requires it.
4. The delegate answers the opportunity-specific questions and uploads the required attachments.
5. The delegate selects Submit and confirms.
6. The system validates mandatory fields, attachments, amounts and the submission window.
7. The system records the application as Submitted at the Reception stage, keeps a snapshot of the Charity and opportunity data and generates the application number.
8. The system shows "Application submitted with number <ref>" and lists it under My applications.

Business rules:
- Project title, requested amount, every field marked mandatory and every required attachment must be completed before submission.
- The requested amount must be greater than zero; when a bill of quantities is used, the requested amount equals the sum of quantity × unit price.
- The submission window is re-checked at the moment of submission.
- The application number is unique: REQ + year-month + sequence (e.g. REQ-2026-10-0042).
- A submitted application is read-only for the Charity unless it is returned for edits (F15).
- The application, its items, attachments and first history entry are saved together; if any part fails, nothing is submitted.

Task Name: S-F11-01 – Fill the application form and save a draft
Description:
As a Charity delegate, I want to fill the opportunity's application form and save it as a draft, so that I can complete it over several sessions.

Note: Draft applications are not visible to Foundation staff.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an open opportunity, when the delegate selects Apply, then the form shows the core fields and the opportunity's own questions in the configured order
2. Given a partly filled form, when the delegate selects Save draft, then the application is saved with status Draft and appears under My applications
3. Given a Draft application, when the delegate reopens it, then all previously entered values and attachments are shown

Task Name: S-F11-02 – Enter the requested amount, duration and bill of quantities
Description:
As a Charity delegate, I want to enter the requested amount, duration and the items with quantities and prices, so that the Foundation sees exactly what is being funded.

Note: Duration is a whole number of days; region from the standard list of 13 regions.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the opportunity requires a bill of quantities, when the delegate adds items, then each line total (quantity × unit price) and the grand total are calculated automatically
2. Given a bill of quantities, then the requested amount equals the grand total and cannot be typed separately
3. Given a requested amount of zero or a negative quantity, when the delegate saves, then the field is rejected with a validation message

Task Name: S-F11-03 – Upload the required attachments
Description:
As a Charity delegate, I want to upload the documents the opportunity requires, so that the application is complete for review.

Note: Allowed: PDF, Word, Excel, image; maximum 10 MB per file.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the opportunity defines required documents, then the form shows one upload slot per document marked Required
2. Given a file of a type or size that is not allowed, when the delegate uploads it, then it is refused with the allowed types and maximum size
3. Given an uploaded attachment, when the delegate removes or replaces it before submission, then only the latest file is kept

Task Name: S-F11-04 – Submit the application and receive its number
Description:
As a Charity delegate, I want to submit the completed application and get a reference number, so that I can follow it up with the Foundation.

Note: A snapshot of the Charity and opportunity data is stored at submission for later review.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a missing required field or attachment, when the delegate selects Submit, then submission is refused and each missing item is listed
2. Given a complete application on an open opportunity, when the delegate confirms Submit, then the status becomes Submitted at the Reception stage and the number REQ-<yyyy-mm>-<sequence> is shown
3. Given a submitted application, then the delegate can view it but every field and attachment is read-only
4. Given the opportunity's close date has passed, when the delegate selects Submit, then submission is refused with "This opportunity is no longer accepting applications"

Task Name: F13 – Application review by stages
Description:
Submitted applications move through Reception → Study → Approval, each stage with named owners, an SLA in days and a task in My Tasks, so every application has a clear owner and a full decision history. Scoring (F14), committee minutes (F16) and AI evaluation (F30) build on this.

Main flow:
1. The system places the submitted application at the Reception stage and creates a task in My Tasks for each stage owner, due on stage entry date + SLA days.
2. The Reviewer opens the review queue, filters by stage and opens the application.
3. The Reviewer studies the dossier: application data, bill of quantities, attachments, Charity profile and history.
4. The Reviewer approves the stage, with an optional note.
5. The system moves the application to the next stage, records who decided and when, removes the old tasks and creates tasks for the next stage's owners.
6. At the Approval stage, the authorised approver gives final approval and the application status becomes Approved.

Business rules:
- Only the stage owners of the current stage, or a Grants Manager, may decide on it; the rule applies from every entry point.
- Closure reasons: No allocated budget / Did not reach the pass score / Outside the opportunity scope / Missing requirements / Other.
- Approval is blocked while edits from the Charity are awaited.
- Each stage entry restarts the SLA clock; task due date = stage entry date + SLA (default 3 days).
- Every action (submission, decision, return, note, attachment) is added to an append-only history with user, stage, note and time.

Detailed BRD: UC59, UC60, UC62, UC88
Ready: Needs decision: Are the three stages fixed, or configurable per opportunity?

Task Name: S-F13-01 – Review queue per stage
Description:
As a Reviewer, I want a queue of applications with filters by stage and status, so that I can find the applications waiting for me.

Note: Search by reference, project title or Charity name.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given submitted applications, when the Reviewer opens the queue, then each row shows reference, project title, Charity, stage, status, requested amount and a Late flag
2. Given the Reviewer filters by stage = Study and status = Pending, then only applications matching both filters are listed
3. Given an application has been at its stage longer than the stage SLA, then it shows the Late flag with the number of days late
4. Given a filtered queue, when the Reviewer exports it, then the Excel file contains exactly the filtered rows

Task Name: S-F13-02 – Application dossier and history
Description: As a Reviewer, I want to see the full application, the Charity's profile and the history on one page, so that I can study it without switching screens.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application, when the Reviewer opens it, then the page shows the application data, bill of quantities, attachments, Charity profile summary, current stage with SLA progress ("x of y days") and the history
2. Given the Reviewer adds a note or a review attachment, then it is saved in the history with user, stage and time
3. Given the history, then entries cannot be edited or deleted by any user

Task Name: S-F13-03 – Stage tasks created automatically
Description:
As a stage owner, I want a task in My Tasks when an application reaches my stage, so that I do not have to watch the queue.

Note: Tasks link directly to the application dossier.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application enters the Study stage with SLA 5 days on 1 March, then each Study owner gets a task due 6 March showing project title, reference, Charity and requested amount
2. Given the application leaves the stage (approved, returned, rejected), then the stage task is removed for all owners without manual closing
3. Given the stage has no SLA configured, then the task due date is stage entry date + 3 days

Task Name: S-F13-04 – Approve a stage
Description: As a stage owner, I want to approve the application at my stage, so that it moves on to the next stage.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application at Reception, when the owner approves, then it moves to Study and the history records the decision, user and time
2. Given an application at the Approval stage, when the authorised approver gives final approval, then its status becomes Approved
3. Given a user who is not an owner of the current stage or a Grants Manager, when they try to decide, then the action is refused and nothing is recorded
4. Given an application with status Awaiting Charity edits, then the Approve action is not available

Task Name: S-F13-05 – Return for edits or reject
Description:
As a stage owner, I want to return an application for edits or reject it with a reason, so that the Charity knows what to do next.

Note: An optional apology message to the Charity may be added on rejection.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the owner selects Return for edits, when no note is entered, then the confirm button stays disabled
2. Given a return with a note, then the status becomes Awaiting Charity edits at the same stage and the note is visible to the Charity
3. Given the owner selects Reject, then a closure reason from the standard list is mandatory, the status becomes Rejected and the Charity receives a notification with the reason

Task Name: F14 – Evaluation criteria and pass score
Description:
Each opportunity has weighted evaluation criteria and a pass score; Reviewers score each criterion, and approval is blocked when the score is below the pass score, so applications are scored consistently and weak ones cannot be approved by mistake.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager adds evaluation criteria with weights to the opportunity and sets the pass score.
2. The system shows the total of the weights and saves only when it equals 100%.
3. The Reviewer opens the application at the Study stage and selects Evaluate.
4. The Reviewer scores each criterion from 0 to 100 and adds a note per criterion.
5. The system calculates the weighted total score and shows it in the dossier and the review queue.
6. When any user tries to approve the Study stage, the system compares the score with the pass score and allows or blocks the approval.

Business rules:
- Criteria weights must total exactly 100%.
- Pass score is between 0 and 100; default 80%.
- Study-stage approval is blocked when the score is missing or below the pass score, from every entry point (application page, task, committee minute).
- Criteria cannot be changed once an application on the opportunity has been scored.

Detailed BRD: UC33

Task Name: S-F14-01 – Define criteria, weights and pass score
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to define weighted evaluation criteria and a pass score for an opportunity, so that all applications are measured the same way.

Note: Pass score defaults to 80%.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given criteria weights totalling 90%, when the Grants Manager saves, then saving is refused and the total is shown in red with "Weights must total 100%"
2. Given weights totalling 100% and a pass score of 75, when saved, then the criteria and pass score are stored on the opportunity
3. Given a pass score above 100 or below 0, then it is refused
4. Given an application on the opportunity has already been scored, then the criteria and weights are read-only

Task Name: S-F14-02 – Score an application
Description:
As a Reviewer, I want to score each criterion with a note, so that my assessment is recorded and comparable.

Note: Weighted total = Σ (criterion score × weight).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application at the Study stage, when the Reviewer enters a score of 0–100 for every criterion and saves, then the weighted total is calculated and shown
2. Given a criterion without a score, then the evaluation cannot be saved
3. Given two Reviewers scored 70 and 90, then the application score shown is 80

Task Name: S-F14-03 – Block approval below the pass score
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want approval blocked when the score is missing or below the pass score, so that weak applications cannot be approved by mistake.

Note: The same check runs from tasks (F27) and committee minutes (F16).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application with score 72% and pass score 80%, when a stage owner approves the Study stage, then approval is refused with "Average score 72% is below the pass score 80%"
2. Given an application with no score, when a stage owner approves the Study stage, then approval is refused with "Enter at least one evaluation before approving the Study stage"
3. Given an application with score 85% and pass score 80%, then the Study stage can be approved

Task Name: S-F14-04 – Show evaluations in the dossier
Description: As a Reviewer, I want to see each Reviewer's scores and notes in the dossier, so that the decision-maker can understand the result.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a scored application, then the dossier shows, per Reviewer, the score per criterion, the notes, the weighted total and the evaluation date
2. Given a Charity delegate views the application in the portal, then no evaluation scores or notes are shown

Task Name: F15 – Charity follow-up and requested edits
Description:
The Charity sees where each application is, edits and resubmits when asked, and accepts or refuses staff-proposed changes to amounts or quantities, so follow-up happens in the portal instead of by phone.

Main flow:
1. The Charity delegate opens My applications and sees each application's reference, opportunity, amount, stage, status and the action required or the expected reply date.
2. When the application is returned for edits, the delegate sees "Edits requested: <reviewer note>".
3. The delegate updates the flagged data or attachments and selects Resubmit.
4. The system returns the application to the same stage, records the resubmission and recreates the stage task.
5. When staff propose new figures, the delegate sees the old and new amount, duration or quantities with the staff note.
6. The delegate accepts the proposal, or refuses it with a reason; the system applies or discards the new figures and records the response.

Business rules:
- Expected reply date = stage entry date + stage SLA days.
- The Charity can edit a submitted application only while its status is Awaiting Charity edits.
- Staff-proposed figures apply only after the Charity accepts; a refusal requires a reason.
- Only one figure proposal may be pending per application; Approve is blocked while it is pending.
- Internal evaluation scores and staff notes (other than the edit-request note) are never shown to the Charity.
- Every resubmission, proposal and response is recorded in the history with before and after values.

Detailed BRD: UC45, UC63

Task Name: S-F15-01 – Track my applications
Description: As a Charity delegate, I want to see the status of each application and what is expected from me, so that I know where it stands without calling the Foundation.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a pending application at Study entered on 1 March with SLA 5 days, then My applications shows stage Study and expected reply 6 March
2. Given an application awaiting Charity action, then the row shows "Action required: <action>" instead of the expected reply date
3. Given a rejected application, then the row shows status Rejected and the closure reason

Task Name: S-F15-02 – Edit and resubmit a returned application
Description:
As a Charity delegate, I want to correct a returned application and resubmit it, so that the review can continue.

Note: The same submission validations as F11 apply on resubmit.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application with status Awaiting Charity edits, then the delegate sees the Reviewer's note and can change the data and attachments
2. Given the delegate selects Resubmit, then the application returns to Pending at the same stage, the history records the resubmission and the stage owners get a new task
3. Given an application that is not Awaiting Charity edits, then its fields are read-only and Resubmit is not shown

Task Name: S-F15-03 – Propose new figures to the Charity
Description: As a Reviewer, I want to propose a new requested amount, duration or quantities, so that the grant matches what the Foundation can fund.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a pending application, when the Reviewer enters a new amount 80,000 (was 100,000) with a note and confirms, then the proposal is sent and the application shows "Figures awaiting Charity response"
2. Given a proposal that changes no figure, when the Reviewer confirms, then it is refused with "No figure was changed"
3. Given a proposal is already pending, then a second proposal cannot be created
4. Given a bill of quantities, when the Reviewer changes quantities, then the new total is recalculated as Σ quantity × unit price

Task Name: S-F15-04 – Accept or refuse proposed figures
Description: As a Charity delegate, I want to accept or refuse the proposed figures, so that the application is only changed with my agreement.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a pending proposal, when the delegate accepts, then the new figures replace the old ones and the history records old and new values
2. Given the delegate selects Refuse without a reason, then the action is blocked with "Enter the reason for refusal"
3. Given the delegate refuses with a reason, then the original figures stay, the proposal is cleared and the Grants Manager gets a follow-up task

Task Name: F16 – Committee decisions by minute
Description:
The Committee Secretary records one committee minute with its signed file and applies its decision to all the applications it covers in one step, so committee decisions are recorded once and every affected application is traceable to the minute.

Main flow:
1. The Secretary selects pending applications of the same committee and stage, from the review queue or My Tasks.
2. The Secretary opens Decide by minute and enters the minute number, minute date and members; the committee name is pre-filled.
3. The Secretary chooses the decision per application: Approve, Reject or Return.
4. The Secretary enters a note (mandatory for Reject) and attaches the signed minute file.
5. The Secretary confirms Apply to n applications.
6. The system stores the minute once and applies each decision under the same rules as an individual decision, including the pass score.
7. The system links every decided application to the minute and shows the number succeeded and failed with the reason for each failure.

Business rules:
- Only the Committee Secretary of the stage can create a minute decision for its applications.
- Minute number, minute date and the signed minute file are mandatory; file types PDF, Word, Excel or image, maximum 10 MB.
- Each application is decided with the same rules as an individual decision: authorisation, pass score, no pending edits or proposals.
- One minute record is stored per decision and linked from the history of every application it decided.
- A finalized minute cannot be edited or deleted.

Detailed BRD: UC64, UC95

Task Name: S-F16-01 – Select applications for a committee minute
Description:
As a Committee Secretary, I want to select several applications of my committee, so that I can decide them together.

Note: Available in the review queue and in My Tasks.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the Secretary ticks a first application, then applications of other committees or stages become unselectable
2. Given n applications are selected, then the selection bar shows "n applications selected" with Decide by minute and Clear selection
3. Given a user who is not the stage's Committee Secretary, then the selection boxes are not shown

Task Name: S-F16-02 – Record the minute with its signed file

As a Committee Secretary, I want to record the minute details and attach the signed minute, so that every decision is backed by the official document.

Note: Minute date defaults to today; committee name pre-filled from the stage set-up.

3. Given Reject is chosen for an application without a note, then Apply is blocked with "Enter the rejection reason in the note"

Task Name: S-F16-03 – Apply the decision to all selected applications
Description: As a Committee Secretary, I want the minute's decisions applied to all selected applications in one step, so that I do not decide each one separately.

Task Name: S-F16-04 – Link decisions to the minute

2. Given a minute, when opened, then it lists the date, members, file and every application with its decision and outcome
