Task Name: E6 – Contracts & Projects
Description: Turn every approved grant into a signed contract and a planned project whose progress is proven with evidence before money is released.

Task Name: F17 – Contract and project from an approved application
Description:
Approved applications are transferred into one contract and one project with the approved amount, cost items and payment schedule, without retyping. The contract is tracked until signed, and execution cannot start before signature.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager opens the approved application and reviews the bill of quantities and payment schedule (instalment title, % of amount, days after start).
2. The Grants Manager adjusts the instalments and saves; the system checks the percentages total 100%.
3. The Grants Manager selects 'Approve contract and transfer' and confirms the project manager.
4. The system creates one contract (status Being prepared) with a unique contract number and the approved amount, and one project (status Planning) with its budget, dates, project manager and scheduled payments.
5. The system marks the application Transferred, records the contract and project references in its history and opens the project.
6. The Grants Manager advances the contract: Being prepared → Awaiting charity → Awaiting signature → Signed, and uploads the signed contract.
7. The charity views and prints the contract in the portal; staff consult the contracts register.

Business rules:
- Exactly one contract and one project per approved application (splitting is out of scope → F33).
- Contract amount = project budget = approved grant amount.
- Instalment percentages must total 100%; instalment amount = % × approved amount.
- Contract status moves forward only; the signature date is recorded when it becomes Signed.
- Bill of quantities and payment schedule become read-only once the application is transferred.
- Project execution cannot start while the contract is not Signed.

Detailed BRD: UC67, UC69, UC70, UC71

Task Name: S-F17-01 – Set the payment schedule
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to define the payment schedule of an approved application as percentages per instalment, so that payments are agreed before the contract is created.

Note: Fields per instalment: title, percentage, due after (days from start); amount is calculated.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given instalments of 20%, 50% and 30% on an approved amount of SAR 100,000, when I save, then the amounts shown are SAR 20,000, 50,000 and 30,000.
2. Given instalments totalling 90%, when I save, then the system refuses with 'Instalment percentages must total 100%' and nothing is saved.
3. Given the application has been transferred, when I open the schedule, then it is read-only.

Task Name: S-F17-02 – Transfer an approved application into a contract and project
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to approve the contract and transfer the application in one step, so that the grant becomes a trackable project without retyping.

Note: Project manager defaults to the opportunity's default manager and can be changed before confirming.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an approved, non-transferred application of SAR 100,000, when I confirm the transfer, then one contract (Being prepared, unique number, SAR 100,000) and one project (Planning, budget SAR 100,000) are created and the application shows Transferred.
2. Given the transfer succeeded, then the project has one scheduled payment per instalment and the application history records the contract and project references.
3. Given the funding plan item's budget is locked, when I confirm, then the system shows 'The budget of <plan> is locked' and no contract, project or payment is created.
4. Given an application already transferred, then the transfer action is not available.

Task Name: S-F17-03 – Track contract signing
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to move the contract through its signing steps and store the signed copy, so that we know which grants are legally binding.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a contract in Being prepared, when I advance it, then it moves to Awaiting charity, then Awaiting signature, then Signed, and never backwards.
2. Given I try to set Signed without uploading the signed contract file, then the system refuses.
3. Given the contract becomes Signed, then the signature date is recorded and shown on the contract and the project.

Task Name: S-F17-04 – View and print the contract
Description: As a Charity user, I want to view and print my contract from the portal, so that I know my obligations and payment schedule.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given my charity has a contract, when I open the project in the portal, then I see the contract parties, value, duration, instalments and bank account, read-only.
2. Given I select Print / PDF, then a printable document without editing controls is produced.
3. Given another charity's contract, when I try to open it, then access is denied.

Task Name: S-F17-05 – Contracts register
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want a register of all contracts, so that I can follow signing status across the portfolio.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the contracts register, then each row shows contract number, charity, application, value, linked project, status and date, with a count per status.
2. Given I click the 'Awaiting signature' count, then only contracts in that status are listed.

Task Name: F18 – Project plan and start of execution
Description:
Each project gets an agreed execution plan of sequential milestones, charity activities, required evidence, due dates and linked payments before work starts. The portfolio list shows every project's status and flags stalled ones.

Main flow:
1. The Project Manager opens the project plan.
2. The Project Manager adds milestones in sequence with a weight (%), and under each milestone the charity activities with due date and required evidence.
3. The Project Manager links each scheduled payment to a milestone.
4. The system shows the milestone weight total and the linked payments total against the project budget.
5. The Project Manager selects 'Approve plan and start execution'.
6. The system checks the start conditions and moves the project to In progress; the first milestone opens for the charity.

Business rules:
- Execution can start only when the contract is Signed, the plan has at least one milestone with at least one activity, milestone weights total 100% and linked payments total the project budget.
- Milestones are sequential: only the current milestone is open; later ones stay locked until the previous one is approved.
- Charity actions are locked while the project is in Planning.
- A project is Stalled when any activity is past its due date and not approved; the same rule applies in counters and on the project page.
- Project progress = weighted average of activity progress.

Detailed BRD: UC72, UC74

Task Name: S-F18-01 – Build the project plan
Description:
As a Project Manager, I want to define milestones, activities, required evidence and due dates, so that the charity knows exactly what to deliver and when.

Note: Activity fields: title, weight, due date, required evidence (one or more named items).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a project in Planning, when I add a milestone with weight 40% and two activities with due dates and required evidence, then they are saved in sequence order.
2. Given milestone weights totalling 90%, then the plan shows the total in red and the warning 'Milestone weights must total 100%'.
3. Given an activity due date after the project end date, when I save, then the system refuses.

Task Name: S-F18-02 – Link payments to milestones
Description:
As a Project Manager, I want to link each scheduled payment to a milestone, so that money is released only when that milestone is proven.

Note: A payment not linked to a milestone (e.g. advance) is allowed and marked as such.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the project's scheduled payments, when I link a payment to a milestone, then the milestone shows the payment title and amount.
2. Given linked payments total less or more than the project budget, then the plan shows the difference and cannot be approved.

Task Name: S-F18-03 – Approve the plan and start execution
Description: As a Project Manager, I want to approve the plan and start execution, so that the charity can begin work against an agreed baseline.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a Signed contract and a complete plan, when I select 'Approve plan and start execution', then the project status becomes In progress and the first milestone becomes open for the charity.
2. Given the contract is not Signed, when I try to start, then the system refuses and lists 'Contract not signed' among the unmet conditions.
3. Given a project In progress, then the plan editing actions are no longer available.

Task Name: S-F18-04 – Project portfolio and stalled flag
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want a projects list with status counters and a stalled flag, so that I can see at a glance which projects need attention.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the projects list, then counters show total, Planning, In progress and Stalled, and clicking a counter filters the list.
2. Given an activity passes its due date without approval, then the project shows Stalled with the reason '<n> overdue items' in the list and on the project page.
3. Given each row, then it shows reference, charity, value, progress %, status and project manager, and the list can be exported to Excel.

Task Name: S-F18-05 – Charity view of its projects
Description: As a Charity user, I want to see my charity's projects with status, progress and plan, so that I know what is expected of us.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given my charity has projects, when I open Projects in the portal, then I see only my charity's projects with reference, status and progress.
2. Given a project in Planning, then I can view it but all activity actions are locked.

Task Name: F19 – Charity progress reports and milestone approval
Description:
The charity uploads evidence for each activity and submits a milestone report in the portal; the Project Manager verifies and approves or returns them. Approving a milestone makes its linked payment due, so money follows proven progress.

Main flow:
1. The charity user opens the current milestone and uploads files for each required evidence item of an activity.
2. The charity user marks the activity complete and submits it for the Grantor's approval.
3. The system creates a verification task for the Project Manager in My Tasks.
4. The Project Manager reviews the evidence and approves the activity or returns it with notes.
5. When all activities are approved, the charity writes and submits the milestone report.
6. The Project Manager approves the report and then the milestone.
7. The system marks the milestone complete, makes its linked payment Due and opens the next milestone.

Business rules:
- An activity can be submitted only when its milestone is open, its prerequisite activities are approved, and each required evidence item has at least one file.
- Evidence files up to 10 MB each.
- Returning an activity or report requires notes.
- Milestone approval is available only for the current milestone, after all its activities and its report are approved.
- A milestone payment stays On hold until its milestone is approved, then becomes Due.
- Only the assigned Project Manager approves activities, reports and milestones.

Detailed BRD: UC47, UC75, UC76

Task Name: S-F19-01 – Submit activity evidence
Description: As a Charity user, I want to upload evidence for an activity and submit it, so that the Grantor can verify our work.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an open activity with two required evidence items, when I upload a file for each and submit, then the activity status becomes Awaiting grantor approval.
2. Given a required evidence item has no file, when I submit, then the system refuses and names the missing item.
3. Given a file larger than 10 MB, when I upload it, then it is rejected with 'File exceeds 10 MB'.
4. Given a milestone that is not yet open, then activity actions are not available.

Task Name: S-F19-02 – Verify evidence and approve or return an activity
Description: As a Project Manager, I want to approve a submitted activity or return it with notes, so that only proven work counts.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a submitted activity, then I have a verification task in My Tasks linking to it.
2. Given I approve the activity, then its status becomes Approved and the dependent activities unlock.
3. Given I return the activity without notes, then the system refuses; with notes, the status becomes Returned and the charity sees the notes.

Task Name: S-F19-03 – Resubmit returned work
Description: As a Charity user, I want to see returned items with the Grantor's notes and resubmit them, so that I can fix issues quickly.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an activity or report was returned, then it appears in my portal inbox with the return notes.
2. Given I correct the evidence and resubmit, then the status becomes Awaiting grantor approval again and the Project Manager gets a new task.

Task Name: S-F19-04 – Submit the milestone report
Description: As a Charity user, I want to submit a progress report for the milestone, so that the Grantor has a summary of what was achieved.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given all activities of the current milestone are approved, when I write the achievement summary and submit, then the report status becomes Awaiting grantor approval.
2. Given the achievement summary is empty, then submit is refused.
3. Given a milestone already has a report awaiting approval or approved, then I cannot submit a second one.

Task Name: S-F19-05 – Approve the milestone and make the payment due
Description: As a Project Manager, I want to approve the report and the milestone, so that the linked payment becomes due and the next milestone opens.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the milestone report is submitted, when I return it, then a reason is mandatory and the charity sees it.
2. Given all activities and the report are approved, when I approve the milestone, then it becomes Complete, its linked payment changes from On hold to Due and the next milestone opens.
3. Given any activity or the report is not approved, then milestone approval is not available.

Task Name: F20 – Plan revisions and project closure
Description:
Changes to a project plan after execution starts go through a reasoned revision request approved by a different person, and projects are closed only after all milestones are approved and a final evaluation is written.

Main flow:
1. The Project Manager opens 'Request plan revision', enters a reason and edits the remaining milestones, activities, dates or payment links.
2. The system shows the differences (added, changed, removed) and checks that total payments do not exceed the project budget.
3. The Project Manager submits the request; an approval task goes to the Grants Manager.
4. A different authorised person approves (optional note) or rejects (mandatory note); on approval the system applies all changes and records the revision.
5. After the last milestone is approved, the Project Manager writes the final evaluation.
6. The Project Manager approves closure; the system sets the project to Closed and the evaluation becomes read-only.

Business rules:
- After execution starts, the plan changes only through an approved revision.
- Approved activities, approved milestones and payments already in approval are never changed by a revision.
- The requester cannot approve their own revision; one pending revision per project.
- A revision is applied completely or not at all; total payments after revision must not exceed the project budget (checked again at approval).
- Closure requires all milestones approved and a non-empty final evaluation.
- A closed project accepts no new activities, revisions or payments.

Detailed BRD: UC77, UC78

Task Name: S-F20-01 – Request a plan revision
Description:
As a Project Manager, I want to propose changes to the remaining plan with a reason, so that the project can adapt in a controlled way.

Note: The request shows differences: added, changed, removed items.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a project In progress, when I submit a revision with a reason of at least 5 characters, then its status is Awaiting approval and the Grants Manager gets a task.
2. Given the revision changes an approved activity or a payment already in approval, then the system refuses that change.
3. Given the revised payments exceed the project budget, then the request cannot be submitted.
4. Given a revision is already Awaiting approval for the project, then 'Request plan revision' is not available.

Task Name: S-F20-02 – Approve or reject a plan revision
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to review the reason and differences and decide, so that only justified changes are applied.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I requested the revision myself, when I try to approve it, then the system refuses.
2. Given I approve, then all changes are applied to the plan in one step and the revision is Approved.
3. Given I reject without a note, then the system refuses; with a note, the plan stays unchanged and the requester sees the note.
4. Given a revision is already decided, then no second decision is possible.

Task Name: S-F20-03 – Revision history
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to see all revisions of a project, so that every change to the agreed plan is documented.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a project with revisions, then the history lists each with requester, approver, dates, reason, decision note and differences.
2. Given a revision was rejected, then it still appears in the history with status Rejected.

Task Name: S-F20-04 – Close the project with a final evaluation
Description:
As a Project Manager, I want to close a completed project with a final evaluation, so that results are documented and the project is locked.

Note: Final evaluation covers impact achieved, adherence to plan and lessons learned.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given any milestone is not approved, then the closure step is locked and lists the open milestones.
2. Given all milestones are approved and the final evaluation is empty, then 'Approve closure' is disabled.
3. Given I approve closure with an evaluation, then the project status becomes Closed and the evaluation is read-only.
4. Given a Closed project, then no activities, revisions or payments can be added.

Task Name: E7 – Payments
Description: Release grant payments only against approved milestones, through a controlled approval chain, to a verified account, and close every payment with proof.

Task Name: F21 – Payment approval chain
Description:
Due payments are submitted for a three-level sequential approval (Project Manager → Grants Manager → CEO) with tasks in My Tasks, so no payment is released without the required approvals.

Main flow:
1. The Project Manager opens the project's due payments list and submits a due payment for approval.
2. The system sets the payment to Awaiting approval (level 1 of 3) and creates a task for the project's Project Manager.
3. The approver opens the task, reviews payment title, amount, due date, level and linked milestone, and approves.
4. The system records the decision and creates the level-2 task for Grants Managers, then the level-3 task for the CEO.
5. When the CEO approves, the payment becomes Approved and is ready for disbursement by Finance.
6. At each step, the decided task is removed from My Tasks.

Business rules:
- Level 1: the project's assigned Project Manager only; level 2: a Grants Manager; level 3: the CEO.
- The same person cannot approve more than one level of the same payment.
- A milestone payment cannot be submitted while its milestone is not approved.
- Every approval and rejection is recorded with level, person, date, decision and reason, visible on the payment.
- The task due date is the payment due date.

Detailed BRD: UC80, UC81, UC89
Ready: Needs decision: Are there amount thresholds that change the approval chain?

Task Name: S-F21-01 – Due payments list and submission
Description: As a Project Manager, I want to see my project's due payments and submit one for approval, so that the charity is paid on time.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a project with payments, then the payments tab lists each with title, amount, due date, linked milestone and status (On hold, Due, Awaiting approval, Approved).
2. Given a Due payment, when I submit it, then its status becomes Awaiting approval – level 1 of 3.
3. Given a payment whose milestone is not approved, then it shows On hold and cannot be submitted.
4. Given an advance payment not linked to a milestone, when an authorised user marks it Due, then it can be submitted.

Task Name: S-F21-02 – Approve a payment step by step
Description: As an approver (Project Manager, Grants Manager or CEO), I want to approve the payment at my level, so that it moves to the next approver.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given level 1 is approved by the project's Project Manager, then the payment moves to level 2 and Grants Managers get the task.
2. Given level 2 is approved, then the CEO gets the level-3 task; when the CEO approves, the payment status becomes Approved.
3. Given I approved level 1 and I also hold the Grants Manager role, when I try to approve level 2 of the same payment, then the system refuses.
4. Given a Project Manager of another project, then they neither see the level-1 task nor can approve it.

Task Name: S-F21-03 – Reject a payment with reason
Description:
As an approver, I want to reject a payment with a reason, so that the Project Manager knows what to fix.

Note: Reason up to 1,000 characters.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I reject without a reason, then the system refuses with 'Rejection reason is required'.
2. Given I reject with a reason, then the payment returns to Due, the reason is shown on the payment, and the open task is removed.
3. Given a rejected payment is resubmitted, then approval restarts at level 1.

Task Name: S-F21-04 – Payment approval tasks and history
Description: As an approver, I want payment approvals in My Tasks and a visible approval history, so that nothing waits unnoticed and every decision is traceable.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a payment reaches my level, then a task with payment title, project, level, amount and due date appears in My Tasks with the due date of the payment.
2. Given a level is decided, then that task disappears for all its holders.
3. Given a payment, then its history shows every approval and rejection with level, person, date and reason.

Task Name: F22 – Disbursement order, transfer and receipt
Description:
After final approval, a numbered disbursement order is issued to Finance, the payee is the charity's verified bank account, Finance records the bank transfer with its notice, and the charity closes the payment by uploading the receipt voucher.

Main flow:
1. The system issues a disbursement order with a unique sequential number and the final approval date, and creates a task for Finance.
2. The Finance Officer opens the order showing charity, project, payment and bank details (bank, account name, IBAN) and every approval of the latest cycle, and prints it.
3. The Finance Officer executes the transfer at the bank, uploads the bank transfer notice, optionally enters the transfer reference and confirms.
4. The system records the transfer date, sets the payment to Awaiting receipt and notifies the charity.
5. The charity user views the transfer notice, uploads the receipt voucher, optionally enters its number and confirms receipt.
6. The system records the receipt date and closes the payment as Paid.

Business rules:
- The payee is the charity's verified bank account by default.
- IBAN must match the Saudi format: SA followed by 22 digits.
- Any payee change after an approval restarts the approval chain; no payee change after transfer is confirmed.
- Transfer cannot be confirmed without at least one transfer notice; receipt cannot be confirmed without at least one receipt voucher.
- Only Finance Officers record transfers; only the charity owning the project confirms receipt.
- Order, transfer notice and voucher stay viewable, read-only, on the paid payment.

Detailed BRD: UC82, UC83, UC84

Task Name: S-F22-01 – Issue the disbursement order
Description: As a Finance Officer, I want a numbered disbursement order for each fully approved payment, so that I pay exactly what was approved.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the CEO approves a payment, then a disbursement order is issued with a unique sequential number and the approval date, the payment status becomes Awaiting transfer and Finance gets a task.
2. Given the order, then it shows charity, project, payment amount and purpose, bank name, account name, IBAN and each approval level with approver name and date.
3. Given the payment was rejected and re-approved, then the order shows only the approvals of the latest cycle.
4. Given I select Print, then the order prints without editing controls.

Task Name: S-F22-02 – Change the payee to a third party
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to direct a payment to a third-party account with justification, so that agreed exceptions are possible and controlled.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I choose Third party without account name, IBAN or justification, then the system refuses to save.
2. Given an IBAN not matching SA + 22 digits, then it is rejected with 'Invalid IBAN'.
3. Given the payee is changed after any approval level, then the approval chain restarts at level 1 and the change is logged with user and time.
4. Given the transfer has been confirmed, then the payee can no longer be changed.

Task Name: S-F22-03 – Record the bank transfer
Description: As a Finance Officer, I want to record the transfer with the bank notice, so that the payment is documented and the charity is informed.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a payment Awaiting transfer, when I confirm without a transfer notice, then the system asks me to attach the bank transfer notice first.
2. Given the charity's bank account is not verified, when I try to confirm, then the system refuses with 'Charity bank account not verified'.
3. Given I upload the notice and confirm, then the transfer date (and reference if entered) is recorded, the status becomes Awaiting receipt and the charity is notified.

Task Name: S-F22-04 – Confirm receipt and close the payment
Description:
As a Charity user, I want to upload the receipt voucher for a transferred payment, so that the payment is closed.

Note: Receipt actions are shown to the charity only when the payment is Awaiting receipt or Paid.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a payment Awaiting receipt, then I can view the transfer notice and upload the receipt voucher.
2. Given I confirm receipt without a voucher, then the system refuses.
3. Given I upload the voucher and confirm, then the receipt date (and number if entered) is recorded and the status becomes Paid.
4. Given a Paid payment, then the disbursement order, transfer notice and voucher are viewable, read-only, by staff and the charity.

Task Name: F23 – Payments register and commitments
Description:
Finance and management see every payment with its status and who it waits for, and each charity's committed, due and paid totals, with Excel export.

Main flow:
1. The user opens the payments register.
2. The system shows summary cards with totals: Overdue (with count), Due, Awaiting approval, Awaiting transfer/receipt, Paid.
3. The system lists payments by due date with number, project, charity, title, amount, due date, due band, status and who it is waiting for.
4. The user clicks a card or filters by status, charity or project.
5. The user exports the filtered list to Excel.
6. The user opens a charity's profile and sees its committed, paid, remaining and due-and-overdue totals.

Business rules:
- One overdue rule everywhere: not Paid, not cancelled, due date before today.
- Waiting on: Project Manager (Due), the current-level approver (Awaiting approval), Finance (Awaiting transfer), the charity (Awaiting receipt).
- Charity committed total = sum of its contract amounts = paid + due + not yet due; cancelled payments excluded.
- 'Paid' follows the single definition agreed in the open decision and is used in every total.
- The export contains exactly the rows of the filtered list.

Detailed BRD: UC79, UC85
Ready: Needs decision: Single definition of “paid” (after transfer or after receipt?)

Task Name: S-F23-01 – Payments register with status cards
Description:
As a Finance Officer, I want one register of all payments with status totals, so that I see what must be paid and what is late.

Note: Due bands: overdue n days, today, within 7 days, within 30 days, more than a month.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the register, then five cards show the total amount for Overdue (with count), Due, Awaiting approval, Awaiting transfer/receipt and Paid.
2. Given a payment not Paid with due date before today, then it shows 'Overdue <n> days' and is counted in the Overdue card.
3. Given I click the Overdue card, then only overdue payments are listed.

Task Name: S-F23-02 – See who each payment waits for
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want each payment to show who it is waiting for, so that I can chase the right person.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a payment at approval level 2, then 'Waiting on' shows 'Grants Manager'.
2. Given a payment Awaiting receipt, then 'Waiting on' shows the charity name.
3. Given I am a Project Manager, then the register shows only payments of my projects.

Task Name: S-F23-03 – Charity commitments
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want each charity's committed, paid, remaining and due-and-overdue totals, so that I know what the Foundation still owes.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a charity with two contracts of SAR 100,000 and 50,000, then its committed total is SAR 150,000 and paid + remaining equals SAR 150,000.
2. Given a cancelled payment, then it is excluded from all the charity's totals.

Task Name: S-F23-04 – Export the register
Description: As a Finance Officer, I want to export the filtered register to Excel, so that I can reconcile with the bank and accounting.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a filtered register of 37 rows, when I export, then the Excel file contains the same 37 rows with the same columns and amounts.
2. Given the export, then amounts are numeric (SAR) and dates are real date values.

Task Name: E8 – Work Management & Insight
Description: Staff see and finish their pending work from one place, and management gets live figures and reports without asking the team.

Task Name: F12 – My Tasks inbox
Description:
Every staff member has one inbox with the tasks assigned to them, their due dates and overdue flags, plus manual tasks and meetings, so no pending work is lost. Bulk decisions and focus mode come later (F27).

Main flow:
1. The system shows the user's open tasks with type, title, assignee, due date and an overdue flag, and the open / completed counts.
2. The user searches by title, description or reference and filters by type: All / Manual / Meetings / Applications / Payments.
3. The user sorts by nearest due date or newest added.
4. The user creates a manual task or meeting, assigns it and sets a due date.
5. The assignee changes the task status (To do → In progress → Done) and adds comments.
6. The user switches to the calendar view to see tasks by due date.

Business rules:
- The inbox combines manual tasks, meetings and system tasks (application stages, later payments) assigned to the user.
- An open task past its due date is flagged overdue with the number of days late, using the Riyadh local date.
- Only the creator or the assignee can edit, change status or delete a manual task; meeting invitees can only view it.
- Task title is required, 1–200 characters; assignee must be an active staff member of the organization (default: me).
- Users see only tasks of their own organization.

Detailed BRD: UC90, UC91, UC92, UC93

Task Name: S-F12-01 – See my tasks with due dates and overdue flags
Description:
As a staff member, I want one list of the tasks assigned to me with their due dates, so that I know what to do first.

Note: Open-task count is shown on the My Tasks menu item.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a task is assigned to the user, then it appears in their inbox with its type, title and due date
2. Given an open task due 3 days ago, then it is flagged "Overdue 3 days"
3. Given the user filters by type Applications, then only application tasks are listed and each type tab shows its count
4. Given sort = nearest due date, then tasks are ordered by due date with undated tasks last

Task Name: S-F12-02 – Create and assign a manual task
Description:
As a staff member, I want to create a task and assign it to myself or a colleague, so that follow-up work is tracked.

Note: Fields: title, description, assignee, due date, status (default To do).
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an empty title or a title over 200 characters, then Save is disabled with "Task title is required and must not exceed 200 characters"
2. Given a valid task assigned to a colleague, when saved, then it appears in the colleague's inbox and in the creator's Assigned by me scope
3. Given a deactivated staff member, then they are not offered as an assignee

Task Name: S-F12-03 – Change status and comment on a manual task
Description: As an assignee, I want to update the status of a task and add comments, so that the creator can follow progress.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the assignee sets the status to Done, then the task leaves the open list, the completed count increases and the completion time is recorded
2. Given a user who is neither creator nor assignee, when they try to change the task, then the action is refused
3. Given a comment is added, then it is shown on the task with author and time to both creator and assignee

Task Name: S-F12-04 – Schedule a meeting
Description: As a staff member, I want to schedule a meeting with date, time, place and attendees, so that it appears in everyone's inbox and calendar.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a meeting with date, time, location or link and two invitees, when saved, then it appears for the organizer and both invitees under Meetings as "Meeting · HH:MM"
2. Given the type is switched back to Task before saving, then time, location and invitees are cleared
3. Given the organizer cancels the meeting, then it is removed from the invitees' inboxes

Task Name: S-F12-05 – Calendar view
Description: As a staff member, I want to see my tasks in a monthly calendar, so that I can plan my workload by date.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the user switches to Calendar, then each task appears on its due date and undated tasks are listed in a separate No date section
2. Given a day has more than three tasks, then three are shown and "+N more" opens the rest

Task Name: F26 – Executive dashboard and reports
Description:
Management sees budget, applications, projects, payments and delays on one dashboard, runs standard reports with Excel export, and reviews staff workload, so they get the numbers without asking the team.

Main flow:
1. The system shows the headline figures: total applications (with pending), approved amount, active projects and paid amount with spend rate.
2. The system shows charts: applications by status and by stage, projects by status, payments by status, and delays.
3. The user opens the reports center and selects a report: applications, projects, payments or charities.
4. The user filters the report, chooses columns and opens a record from a row.
5. The user exports the report to Excel.
6. The Grants Manager opens a staff member's profile to see their workload and performance.

Business rules:
- Every figure is calculated from the same registers it summarises (applications, projects, payments register) and matches them.
- "Paid" uses the same definition as the payments register (F23).
- All figures and reports are limited to the user's organization.
- An export contains exactly the filtered rows and visible columns.
- Staff performance is visible only to the Grants Manager, CEO and Admin.

Task Name: F27 – Productivity tools
Description:
Global search, saved list views and exports, decisions directly from tasks (including bulk decisions) and a focus mode help staff spend less time navigating and deciding, without bypassing any business rule.

Main flow:
1. The user opens global search (search icon or Ctrl/Cmd+K) and types at least two characters.
2. The system returns matching Charities, applications, projects and payments the user may access, grouped by type.
3. On a list page the user sets filters and columns, saves them as their default view and exports the list.
4. In My Tasks the user selects Approve, Return or Reject directly on an application or payment task.
5. The system shows a decision summary, applies the same rules as on the record and removes the task when decided.
6. The user starts focus mode and processes open tasks one at a time.

Business rules:
- Search results and exports include only records the user's role and organization may access.
- Decisions from a task, bulk selection or focus mode apply exactly the same rules as on the record (authorisation, pass score, pending edits, payment approval chain).
- Return and reject always require a reason of up to 1000 characters.
- Saved views are personal and kept across devices; search text is not saved.
- Focus mode excludes meetings and shows tasks ordered by due date.

Task Name: S-F27-01 – Global search
Description:
As a staff member, I want to search across Charities, applications, projects and payments from any page, so that I reach a record in seconds.

Note: Search by name, title and reference number.
Acceptance Criteria:

2. Given a record the user's role may not access, then it never appears in the results

Task Name: S-F27-02 – Saved views and list exports

As a staff member, I want to save my filters and columns as my default view and export any list, so that I do not set them up every time.

Task Name: S-F27-03 – Decide directly from a task
Description: As a Reviewer, I want to approve, return or reject from my task list, so that I do not open each record for simple decisions.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the user selects Approve on an application task, then a summary with Charity, amount, score and a link to the full application is shown before confirmation
2. Given an application with score 70% and pass score 80%, when approved from the task, then the decision is refused with the pass-score message and the task stays

Task Name: S-F27-04 – Bulk decisions
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to apply the same decision to several selected tasks, so that I clear routine approvals quickly.

Note: Committee-stage items are decided by minute (F16), not by bulk decision.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the user selects tasks of different types or stages, then the bulk decision is not offered
2. Given 6 selected tasks approved in bulk where 1 fails a rule, then 5 are decided and the result shows "Succeeded: 5 · Failed: 1" with the reason
3. Given a bulk reject, then one reason is mandatory and recorded on every decided item

Task Name: S-F27-05 – Focus mode
Description:
As a staff member, I want to process my open tasks one by one in a focus view, so that I work through my queue without distraction.

Note: Meetings are excluded from focus mode.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the user starts focus mode, then the first open task by due date is shown with "Done today N", "Remaining N" and time on task
2. Given a manual task, when the user selects Complete, then it is marked Done and the next task is shown
3. Given at least two tasks remain, when the user selects Skip, then the task moves to the end of the queue; with one task left Skip is not available
4. Given no tasks remain, then the system shows "No tasks remaining" and the number completed today

Task Name: E9 – Advanced Grants & AI
Description: Extend the working grant core with AI assistance and additional grant models (in-kind, tendered, multi-project) while people keep every decision.

Task Name: F30 – AI assistance
Description:
AI saves time on application forms, document checks and evaluation, and answers questions on grant data, while people confirm every value and take every decision.

Main flow:
1. The charity user uploads a document on the application form and selects 'Fill with AI'; the system shows proposed values marked as AI-proposed.
2. The charity user reviews, edits and confirms; only confirmed values are saved.
3. On each uploaded attachment, the system runs an advisory AI check and shows a verdict and issues.
4. The External AI Evaluation Agent sends an evaluation report (score, criteria, summary, recommendation) for an application; the system validates and stores it.
5. The reviewer reads the AI evaluation in the dossier and records their own opinion; a contradicting opinion needs a justification.
6. A staff user asks the AI assistant a question; it answers from data the user may access and proposes links to pages where any action is confirmed.

Business rules:
- AI output is advisory: nothing is saved, approved or blocked by AI without a person's action.
- The AI assistant is read-only and uses only the user's organization data within their permissions, decided by the system.
- Evaluation reports are accepted only from an authenticated agent of the same Foundation; overall score 0–100, criterion scores 0–10 (max 50 criteria).
- AI evaluation results are visible to grants staff only, never to charities.
- Every AI request and received report is logged (user or agent, time, application or data area).

Detailed BRD: UC05, UC48, UC61
Ready: Needs decision: Which AI provider, and what data may be sent to it?

Task Name: S-F30-01 – AI pre-fill of application forms
Description: As a Charity user, I want AI to propose form values from my uploaded documents, so that I fill the application faster.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I upload a document and select 'Fill with AI', then proposed values appear in the form marked as AI-proposed.
2. Given I leave the form without confirming, then no proposed value is saved.
3. Given I edit a proposed value and confirm, then my edited value is saved.

Task Name: S-F30-02 – Advisory AI document check
Description: As a Reviewer, I want an AI check on each attachment, so that I spot wrong or weak documents early.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an attachment is uploaded, then the dossier shows the AI verdict (OK / Flagged) with the issues found.
2. Given a document is flagged, then the user can still submit or approve, after a confirmation prompt.
3. Given the AI check is unavailable, then the attachment is accepted and marked 'Not checked'.

Task Name: S-F30-03 – Receive external AI evaluation reports
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want the external evaluation agent to post its report on an application, so that reviewers get a structured AI evaluation.

Note: Fields: score 0–100, colour band, label (≤80 chars), summary (≤2,000), recommendation (≤200), criterion scores.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a report with valid agent credentials and a known application reference, then it is stored with the time received and logged in the application history.
2. Given an overall score of 120 or a criterion score of 11, then the report is rejected with the list of problems.
3. Given invalid credentials or an application of another Foundation, then the report is rejected.

Task Name: S-F30-04 – Use the AI evaluation in review
Description: As a Reviewer, I want to read the AI evaluation and record my own opinion, so that AI informs but does not replace my judgement.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application with an AI evaluation, then the dossier shows score, label, recommendation, summary and per-criterion scores; the charity never sees them.
2. Given my opinion contradicts the AI recommendation, when I save without a justification, then the system refuses.
3. Given one or more reviewers decided against the AI recommendation, then the decision-maker sees a warning with the count.

Task Name: S-F30-05 – AI assistant for grant questions
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to ask questions about grant data in Arabic, so that I get answers without building reports.

Note: Charity users have no access to the assistant.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I ask 'Which payments are due this month?', then the answer lists figures from actual data in SAR with Western digits.
2. Given data outside my permissions, then the assistant does not use or reveal it.
3. Given a change is needed, then the assistant shows a link to the page where I confirm it; it never changes records itself.
4. Given any request, then it is logged with user, time, question and data areas read.

Task Name: F31 – In-kind grants
Description:
The Foundation can grant products from its own stock, not only money: products are offered through product opportunities, charities request quantities, approval deducts stock and delivery is recorded.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager maintains the product catalog: name, description, unit, unit price and stock.
2. The Grants Manager creates a product opportunity and ticks the catalog products offered.
3. The charity user submits a product request with quantities per product.
4. The request is reviewed and scored like other applications.
5. At final approval the system checks stock, deducts the approved quantities and sets the grant to Awaiting delivery.
6. After handover, the Grants Manager records the delivered quantities; the grant becomes Delivered.

Business rules:
- Product name and unit are mandatory; unit price and stock are zero or more.
- Each product appears at most once per opportunity.
- Stock is deducted once, at final approval, and never becomes negative.
- A product referenced by any request cannot be deleted, only archived.
- In-kind grants do not create contracts or payments.

Detailed BRD: UC35, UC68

Task Name: S-F31-01 – Maintain the product catalog
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to manage products with unit, price and stock, so that we know what we can grant.

Note: Units: unit, device, basket, session, month, kilo, book, licence.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I add a product without a name, then the system refuses with 'Product name is required'.
2. Given a product referenced by a request, when I try to delete it, then the system offers only Archive.
3. Given the catalog, then each product shows name, unit, unit price and current stock.

Task Name: S-F31-02 – Offer products in an opportunity
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to select catalog products for a product opportunity, so that charities can request them.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a product opportunity, when I tick products, then they are offered with unit price and available stock.
2. Given a product already on the opportunity, then it cannot be added twice.

Task Name: S-F31-03 – Request products
Description: As a Charity user, I want to request quantities of offered products, so that I receive goods for my beneficiaries.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given I request 50 units of a product with 30 in stock, then the request is refused with 'Requested quantity of <product> exceeds available (30)'.
2. Given I submit without any product quantity, then the system refuses with 'Select at least one product and quantity'.
3. Given a valid request, then it enters review with total value = Σ quantity × unit price.

Task Name: S-F31-04 – Approve and deliver an in-kind grant
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want approval to deduct stock and to record delivery, so that stock is accurate and delivery is tracked.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given final approval of 20 units with 30 in stock, then stock becomes 10 and the grant is Awaiting delivery.
2. Given stock fell below the approved quantity, then final approval is blocked with the product name and available quantity.
3. Given a grant Awaiting delivery, when I record delivered quantities, then it becomes Delivered and the history records the delivery; stock is not deducted again.
4. Given an approved in-kind grant, then no contract transfer is offered.

Task Name: F32 – Tendered projects (RFP)
Description:
The Foundation can tender a defined project, receive offers from invited charities, compare them side by side and award the best evaluated offer, which then becomes a contract and project.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager enters scope of work, deliverables, duration, weighted activities and payment milestones (% of winning amount, days after award).
2. The system checks activity weights and payment percentages each total 100% and publishes the details to invited charities.
3. Invited charities submit technical and financial offers.
4. Reviewers evaluate offers against the criteria and pass score.
5. The Grants Manager compares offers side by side and selects 'Award' on one evaluated, passing offer.
6. The system awards it, closes all other offers with a notice, and creates the contract and project with activities and payments.

Business rules:
- Activity weights and payment percentages must each total 100%.
- The opportunity budget is the financial ceiling for offers.
- Only one offer per RFP can be awarded, and only a pending offer that was evaluated and passed.
- Payments = milestone % × winning amount; due dates counted from the award date.
- The award is all-or-nothing.

Detailed BRD: UC37

Task Name: S-F32-01 – Define the tendered project
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to define the scope, deliverables, activities and payment milestones of a tender, so that charities bid on the same requirements.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given activity weights totalling 95%, when I save, then the system refuses with 'Activity weights must total 100%'.
2. Given payment percentages totalling 110%, then the system refuses with 'Payment percentages must total 100%'.
3. Given valid details, then invited charities see them in the portal.

Task Name: S-F32-02 – Submit an offer
Description: As a Charity user, I want to submit a technical and financial offer to an RFP I am invited to, so that I can compete for the project.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a budget ceiling of SAR 500,000, when I submit a financial offer of SAR 520,000, then it is refused with 'Financial offer exceeds the ceiling (500,000)'.
2. Given I am not invited, then I cannot see or bid on the RFP.
3. Given a valid offer, then it appears to staff with status Pending.

Task Name: S-F32-03 – Compare offers
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to see offers side by side, so that I can choose the best value.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given several offers, then each card shows charity, financial offer, average evaluation score against the pass score and status, and the lowest financial offer is marked.
2. Given an offer not yet evaluated, then it shows 'Not evaluated' and cannot be awarded.

Task Name: S-F32-04 – Award the RFP
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to award the best evaluated offer, so that the project starts with the winning charity.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an offer below the pass score, then Award is not available.
2. Given I award a passing offer of SAR 450,000 with milestones 30%/70%, then a contract and project of SAR 450,000 are created with payments of SAR 135,000 and 315,000.
3. Given an award, then all other offers are closed as Not awarded and their charities receive the notice 'Thank you for your interest; the project was awarded to another offer'.
4. Given an RFP already awarded, then no second award is possible.

Task Name: F33 – Multi-project grants, merges and funding conditions
Description:
Complex grants are handled without workarounds: one application can be split into several projects, applications of the same charity can be merged, co-funding conditions and indicators are tracked, and the Foundation can run internal initiatives.

Main flow:
1. The Grants Manager registers co-funders with their contribution as Confirmed or as an approval condition, attaching the donor's approval when received.
2. The Grants Manager links plan indicators to the application with a required quantity.
3. To merge, the Grants Manager selects pending or approved applications of the same charity and grant type; the system shows the impact and builds one merged application.
4. At transfer, the Grants Manager chooses Split and assigns each cost item to a named project; each project's budget is the sum of its items.
5. The system creates one contract and the projects, carrying co-funding and indicators over.
6. Separately, the Grants Manager creates an internal initiative run by the Foundation, in Planning status.

Business rules:
- Split projects' budgets total the approved amount; split needs ≥2 cost items and every project ≥1 item.
- Merging is allowed only for applications of the same charity and grant type, not transferred and not already merged; merged applications produce one contract.
- A co-funding condition becomes confirmed only with the donor's approval evidence attached.
- An indicator cannot be linked beyond its remaining target across all applications and projects.
- Internal initiatives need a name, a budget > 0 and an end date not before the start date.

Detailed BRD: UC65, UC66, UC73

Task Name: S-F33-01 – Split an application into several projects
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to split an approved application into several projects, so that distinct components are managed separately.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application with one cost item, then the Split option is not available.
2. Given a project in split mode has no cost item, then confirmation is disabled with 'Each project needs at least one item'.
3. Given a split of SAR 300,000 into two projects, then one contract of SAR 300,000 and two projects whose budgets total SAR 300,000 are created.

Task Name: S-F33-02 – Merge applications of the same charity
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to merge several applications of one charity, so that they are decided and contracted as one grant.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given applications of different charities, then the merge is refused with 'Applications belong to different charities'.
2. Given a valid merge, then one merged application with the total amount is created and the absorbed applications are closed with 'Merged into <ref>'.
3. Given the merge would move a finally approved application back into review, then a second confirmation is required.
4. Given the merged application's contract has moved past Being prepared, then unmerge is not available.

Task Name: S-F33-03 – Co-funding conditions
Description: As a Grants Manager, I want to record co-funders and their approval conditions, so that we do not approve a grant whose co-funding is not secured.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a co-funder without a name or with amount 0, then the system refuses with 'Enter donor name and amount'.
2. Given a co-funding condition without the donor's approval attached, when final approval is attempted, then it is blocked.
3. Given I attach the donor's approval, then the condition becomes Confirmed and is logged in the history.

Task Name: S-F33-04 – Link plan indicators
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to link plan indicators with target quantities to an application, so that grant results roll up to the plan.

Note: Milestone-type indicators are linked with a target of 1.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an indicator with 40 remaining, when I link 50, then the system refuses with 'Only 40 remain for this indicator'.
2. Given the application is transferred, then indicators can no longer be changed from the application and are carried to the project(s).

Task Name: S-F33-05 – Create an internal initiative
Description:
As a Grants Manager, I want to create an initiative run by the Foundation, so that internal work is followed like grant projects.

Note: Executor can be internal or a registered charity.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a name and a budget of SAR 80,000, when I save, then the initiative is created in Planning with me as project manager by default and appears in the projects list as source Initiative.
2. Given a budget of 0 or an end date before the start date, then the system refuses with the specific error.
